items.title: More Americans are about to get scammed by the coming peptide rush
items.content: Patients will order these cheaper, unproven products via an 800-number or the internet, skipping appointments with real doctors who can provide accurate diagnoses and proven treatments.

items.title: Warren Buffett exits Berkshire Hathaway as his son Howard becomes chairman
items.content: Warren Buffett, the investing legend that turned Berkshire Hathaway into an massive conglomerate, has officially stepped aside as chairman after leaving as CEO at the beginning of the year.

items.title: The Fed’s never been so confident on economic growth. What investors should do now, according to KKR.
items.content: Members of the Federal Open Market Committee showed their lowest level of worry about gross domestic product growth since it first started releasing its outlook.

items.title: The Fed hasn’t been this terse since 2007. What a 130-word statement signals for market stability.
items.content: Bank of America calculates this week’s Federal Open Market Committee statement explaining the decision to lift interest rates by a quarter-point as its most terse, at just 130 words, since 2007.

items.title: I’m in my 50s. My mother died from Alzheimer’s. Do I need long-term insurance?
items.content: “By the time my mother died, the insurance company had paid out almost $600,000.”

items.title: The 10-year Treasury is having its worst run in over 100 years. Why investors are buying bonds anyway.
items.content: “The higher that yields go — for at least new money — it becomes more enticing to think about putting money into bonds,” one strategist notes.

items.title: Micron, Intel and other chip stocks are furthering their strong comebacks
items.content: Investor fears about an AI spending slowdown and the impact of interest-rate hikes are subsiding.

items.title: Wall Street is betting Trump backs down on Iran — but what if the ‘TACO’ trade fails this time?
items.content: For six months, investors had a playbook: when Trump threatens Iran, buy the dip, because he always backs down. But in September, the playbook stopped working.

items.title: Tesla’s upcoming product frenzy could leave investors disappointed
items.content: Slower-than-expected robotaxi progress is still a chief concern, according to experts.
